title: U.S. House · Alabama's 4th Congressional District
area: North-central and northwest Alabama, a largely rural district including Cullman, Jasper, Gadsden, and the Shoals area.

context.text: Incumbent Robert Aderholt (R) defeated Tommy Barnes 77.6% to 22.4% in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary; Amanda Pusczek defeated Shane Weaver 62.8% to 37.2% in the Democratic primary. Cook Political Report rated the district R+33 for 2026, the most heavily Republican in the state.

candidates.name: Robert Aderholt
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary, 77.6% to 22.4%, over Tommy Barnes.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Alabama's 4th Congressional District (since 1997)

priorities.text: Says American leadership requires maintaining the strongest military in the world, strengthening alliances such as NATO, and leading in defense technology, cybersecurity, and space research, citing North Alabama's role in that work.
Says Congress should cut spending and live within a budget rather than raise taxes, calling this the responsible way to address the federal fiscal situation.

positions.summary: Says gun owners' rights should be expanded rather than restricted, and says he cosponsored H.R. 822, the National Right-To-Carry Reciprocity Act, in the 112th Congress.
positions.quote: I firmly believe that we need to expand the rights of gun owners rather than seeking new ways to impose restrictions.

positions.summary: Opposed the Affordable Care Act (Obamacare) and says the House has voted numerous times to repeal it, citing new taxes on health care providers and the individual mandate.
positions.quote: I opposed the President's healthcare bill, the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (PPACA), also known as Obamacare.

positions.summary: Says he believes in looking for ways to curb and stop abortions in the United States.
positions.quote: I also wholeheartedly believe that we should look for ways to curb and stop abortions in the United States.

positions.summary: Cosponsored H.R. 28, the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act of 2025, which would recognize sex in school athletics under Title IX based solely on reproductive biology and genetics at birth.

record.text: Chairs the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies in the 119th Congress (2025-2026); also serves on the Defense and Agriculture, Rural Development subcommittees.
Chaired the same Labor-HHS-Education Appropriations Subcommittee in the 118th Congress (2023-2024) and also served on the Commerce, Justice, Science and Defense subcommittees.

candidates.researchNotes: Aderholt has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and no distinct 2026 campaign issues page was found; positions and priorities are drawn from the issue pages on his official House site, which mix longstanding and recent statements (dated where the page itself gives a date).

candidates.name: Amanda Pusczek
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary, 62.8% to 37.2%, over Shane Weaver.

priorities.text: Says healthcare workers' voices are too often missing from the legislative process and that their perspective is needed to create policies that ensure affordable, quality care.
Supports raising taxes on earners making over a million dollars and closing capital-gains loopholes to fund public services.

positions.summary: Says raising taxes on earners over a million dollars and closing capital-gains loopholes is essential for a fair economy.
Ballotpedia survey response lists "Expand Medicaid and move towards Universal Healthcare" and reversing Medicaid cuts among her campaign priorities.
positions.quote: Expand Medicaid and move towards Universal Healthcare

positions.summary: Ballotpedia survey response lists "End current ICE funding" among her campaign priorities.
Ballotpedia survey response lists codifying Roe v. Wade among her campaign priorities.
Ballotpedia survey response lists investing in green energy among her campaign priorities.

candidates.researchNotes: Birthplace differs between her campaign website and news (Missouri) and her Ballotpedia survey profile (Alabama); the campaign site is used. Nursing associate degree year is 2014 per Ballotpedia; no campaign page gives a year.
